supersedes_nothing: This ADDS to analysis/xsp/xsp-feasibility-2026-09-02.json. It does not replace its verdict; it corrects one input to it.
why_this_sample_exists: The feasibility doc names ONE measurement that would settle the XSP question -- XSP vs SPY NBBO at matched ATM strikes during RTH -- and explicitly discounts its own data point because it was taken at 06:42 ET with the market CLOSED, 'which is exactly when quotes are least representative, so it is recorded and not relied on'. This is the first sample taken inside a live session.

the_prior_number_it_corrects.status_now: REFUTED as a spread estimate. It measured closed-market quotes, not tradeable ones.

sample.contracts: SPY260902C00765000 vs XSP260902C00765000 -- same strike, same 0DTE expiry

what_it_shows.absolute_spread: IDENTICAL at $0.05 on both. The 29x figure was an artifact of the closed market.
what_it_shows.relative_spread: XSP is TIGHTER as a share of premium: 0.05/2.195 = 2.3% vs SPY 0.05/1.005 = 5.0%.
what_it_shows.depth_is_the_real_difference: SPY quotes 345x59 at the touch; XSP quotes 10x10. That is 6-35x thinner, and depth -- not spread -- is what the feasibility doc was actually worried about ('the ability to get out').
what_it_shows.volume: XSP 10,000 vs SPY 422,538 = 2.4% (the feasibility doc's estimate was 8-12%; this session is thinner than that).
what_it_shows.for_THIS_engine_at_THIS_size: The tight ladder caps entries at 5 contracts (max_contracts_per_entry) with a $1,000 position cap. Both sides quote >= 10 at the touch, so a 3-5 lot clears at the touch on either instrument. The execution penalty the feasibility verdict assumed -- '$0.04 of extra spread on a 3-lot already eats' the ~$10/trade tax edge -- is NOT present in this sample.

caveats_that_bound_this_sample: n=1. The feasibility doc asks for every 5 min across 3+ RTH sessions. One quote pair at 14:25 ET is a data point, not the study. It is recorded so the study has a real starting value instead of a closed-market one.

THE STRIKES MAY NOT BE MONEYNESS-MATCHED, and this is an INFERENCE, not a measurement. The same 765 strike quotes 2.17/2.22 on XSP against 0.98/1.03 on SPY. If time value is comparable, that implies XSP spot sits roughly $1.20 ABOVE SPY -- consistent with XSP tracking SPX/10 while SPY carries a tracking/dividend difference. XSP is an index and is NOT in Alpaca's equity quote feed (get_stock_latest_quote returned SPY only), so its spot could not be read directly to confirm. A properly matched study must resolve XSP spot and select each side's true ATM strike independently rather than reusing one strike number.
A single mid-afternoon sample says nothing about the open or the close, which is where 0DTE spreads are widest and where this engine actually trades (entries 09:35-15:00).
Depth at the touch is not depth through the book. 10x10 displayed does not mean only 10 available, and 345x59 does not mean 345 fillable at that price.
what_this_does_NOT_change: The feasibility verdict was PROBABLY NOT WORTH A LANE on three legs: cash-settlement (TRUE), a small ~$10/trade tax edge (TRUE), and a FALSE sizing premise. Only the execution-penalty leg is touched here, and only weakened -- the tax edge no longer has to beat a 29x spread, but it still has to beat a genuinely thinner book and a 2.4%-volume instrument. This sample makes the question OPEN again; it does not make the answer yes.
next: Wire the recurring sampler the feasibility doc actually asked for -- matched TRUE-ATM strikes resolved per side, every 5 min across 3+ RTH sessions including the first and last 30 minutes -- and express the result as $/round-trip on a 3-lot. Until then this stays a single observation.
